sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 172. Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper on votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election:

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body: Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper on votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election:

sections.heading: Exceptions and provisos
sections.body: Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a person who has been authorised to vote as proxy for an elector under any law for the time being in force in so far as he votes as a proxy for such elector

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 172 (Personation at elections), Chapter IX — Of Offences Relating to Elections.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper on votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election:
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 172 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 172 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Introduction. BNS s. 172 deals with Personation at elections. It sits in Chapter IX — Of Offences Relating to Elections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Personation at elections. BNS restatement of IPC 171D. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 171D. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 172 is the rule on “Personation at elections”. The section provides that whoever at an election applies for a voting paper on votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election:. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper on votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election:

Conclusion. BNS s. 172 is the complete current-law heading for Personation at elections. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 172 constitutes a key component of Chapter IX (Of Offences Relating to Elections) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing personation at elections. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of personation at elections under Section 172 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 172.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 172 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 172 vs General Attempt: Section 172 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter IX; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 172 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 172 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Relating to Elections.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 172 for conduct relating to personation at elections.
Rule: Under BNS s. 172, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 172.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 172 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
